title: Thales' Theorem
description: Explore why an angle subtended by a diameter is always a right angle.

title: Angle at the Centre Theorem
description: Demonstrate that the angle subtended by an arc at the centre is twice the angle subtended at the circumference.

title: Angles in the Same Segment
description: Explore how angles subtended by the same chord or arc in the same segment of a circle are equal.

title: Cyclic Quadrilateral Theorem
description: Verify that opposite angles of an inscribed cyclic quadrilateral sum to exactly 180 degrees.

title: Tangent-Radius Perpendicularity
description: Investigate why a tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

title: Alternate Segment Theorem
description: Visualize how the angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle subtended in the alternate segment.

title: Tangents from an External Point
description: Discover why the two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length and subtend equal angles at the centre.

title: Perpendicular Chord Bisector
description: Demonstrate that the perpendicular line from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

title: Unit Circle, Six Trig Functions & 3D Helix Waves
formula: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1  |  r(θ) = (R cos θ, R sin θ, kθ)
description: Explore all six trigonometric functions (sin, cos, tan, sec, csc, cot) as geometric segments on the 2D unit circle and as orthogonal wave projections of a 3D cylindrical helix.

title: Law of Sines & Circumcircle Invariant
formula: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C = 2R
description: Verify why the ratio of any triangle chord to the sine of its opposite inscribed angle is strictly constant and equal to the circumcircle diameter 2R in 2D and 3D.

title: Law of Cosines & Generalized Pythagorean Projection
description: Decompose any acute, right, or obtuse triangle via idempotent orthogonal projection and see how the 2ab cos C interaction rectangle generalizes Pythagoras' theorem.

title: Angle Sum, Difference & Rotation Matrix Composition
description: Discover how composing 2D and 3D rotation matrices R(α) and R(β) geometrically proves the compound angle identities for sin(α ± β) and cos(α ± β).
